params.body:
Six tasks in the fleet say "set DNS records" and stop there. The work is one line of text in a registrar's panel, and this scan already knows what that line needs: which providers send in this name, where the MX points, what is missing. Keeping that in our heads makes a person work out twice what was measured once.

- `dmarcDraft`: `v=DMARC1; p=none` when there is no policy. It holds nothing back and only shows what is being sent in the name; whoever tightens to quarantine later does it with reports in hand rather than blind.
- `spfDraft`: the includes of every provider the scan can actually see (by include or DKIM selector), ending in `~all` so an unseen sender lands in spam rather than bouncing. **Null when it cannot be known**: no recognised sender, or an MX pointing somewhere none of them owns — a SPF that misses a real sender puts that sender's mail in the spam folder, which is worse than no suggestion.

A draft, never a hand: DNS is the one place where a wrong line stops a whole company's mail, and no grant here reaches a registrar.

664 tests, PHPStan, Pint.
params.title: De regel om te plakken, als we hem kunnen weten
